This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner for compensation of Rs. 50,00,000/- and to direct the respondents to provide an employment to the petitioner in any of the Government Departments suitable to the petitioner's educational qualification within the time stipulated by this Hon'ble Court and pass such further orders.
2.According to the petitioner, she married one Vivekananda Kumar and their marriage took place at Vedasanthur on 09.02.2017.
After marriage, the petitioner along with her husband lived in Madurai.
On 30.10.2017, a male child was born to them.
The petitioner's husband was running a shop at Simmakkal, Madurai in the name of 'Sri Saai Traders' by dealing in old tyres business.

On 15.06.2019, the petitioner's husband while proceeding in his two wheeler bearing Registration No.TN-64-S-2302 along with his employee namely Saravana Kumar at about 11.30 p.m, when they were crossing the Vaigai River Bridge, the Police officials belonging to the Delta force of the third r e s p o n d e n t s u d d e n l y s h o w e d h i s h a n d t o s t o p t h e b i k e a n d t h e f o u r t h https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis respondent struck her husband in the chest with his lathi, thereby,
her husband fell down from the bike.
Due to that blow from the lathi, he fell down from the bike and sustained injuries.
Thereafter, he was taken through ambulance and admitted in the hospital.
On 16.06.2019, at about 12.15 a.m, in spite of giving better treatment to her husband, he died in the evening of 16.06.2019, due to the acts done by the police officials.
The petitioner's husband died and sustained multiple injuries all over the body.

An FIR was registered in Crime No.108 of 2019, on the file of Traffic Investigation Wing-I, Madurai City, under Sections 279 and 337 of IPC and thereafter,
sections were altered to Section 304A.
3.The fourth respondent who was identified as the person to struck the blow and was suspended from the Police force.
The fourth respondent and other Police men have arrayed as respondents 1 to 3.
The occurrence had happened because of the respondents, thereby, all the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The petitioner lost her husband in her young age and she has 1  year old child and father-in-law depending on the deceased.
Deceased was aged about 40 years at the time of accident and he was doing old tyres business.

On 12.07.2019, the petitioner sent a representation seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- and an employment in the Government s e r v i c e . N o a c t i o n h a s b e e n t a k e n s o f a r . T h e r e f o r e , s h e f i l e d t h i s p e t i t i o n .
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

4.The respondents filed a status report stating that pursuant to the order of this Court, the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Traffic, Madurai City took up the case for further investigation and filed a final report against Head Constable K.Ramesh Babu for the offences under Sections 304(ii) and 308 IPC on 19.07.2022 and the same was taken on file by the Judicial Magistrate No.I, Madurai in P.R.C.No.241 of 2022.
The case was committed to the file of the Sessions Court and now transferred to V Additional Sessions Court, Madurai.

This Court by an order dated 02.11.2022, in Crl.O.P.No.1163 of 2020 directed to complete the trial of the said case, within a period of six V.Gajapriya vs The Government Of Tamil Nadu on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9734366/
2 months.

sentences.text: Further, this Court vide its order dated 02.11.2022 in WP(MD).No.18475 of 2019 ordered the Home Department to take a decision, within a period of four weeks regarding payment of compensation to the petitioner for the death of her husband, as a result of gross negligent Act on the part of the Head Constable from the date of receipt of a copy of the order and to report before this Court for passing further orders.
5.Accordingly, the Government was addressed through the Director General of Police, HoPF, Tamil Nadu, Chennai for taking decision on the payment of compensation through letter dated 16.05.2023.

The Government after examining the report, in the light of the compensation awarded by the Government in certain cases involving death due to physical assault by the Police issued a Government order in G.O.(D).No.481 dated 02.05.2023 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis sanctioning the compensation of sum of Rs.3,00,000/- to the petitioner and administrative process for disbursing this amount to the petitioner is under process and the Director General of Police,
HoPF, Tamil Nadu, Chennai has been requested to issue necessary proceedings for withdrawal and disburse of the compensation amount to the petitioner vide letter dated 16.05.2023.

6.Further, the victim T.Vivekanantha Kumar was found driving the two wheeler in an inebriated condition when the occurrence took place and driven the vehicle in a negligent manner without wearing helmet.

Based on the findings of the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Traffic, Madurai City necessary disciplinary proceedings were initiated against the Police Officers of Mr.S.Rathinavelu,
SSI, Tmt.Latha, WSI, Tmt.G.Jansi Rani, Inspector and Mr.Justin Prabhakaran, Assistant Commissioner of Police, CCB, Madurai City for negligence on their part in connection with the above incident.
In this connection, the Deputy Commissioner of Police, North, Madurai City has been directed to conduct personal enquiry for taking further necessary action.

7.The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would contend that the petitioner's husband was doing old tyres business and on 15.06.2019, at about 11.30 p.m, when he along with one Saravana Kumar proceeding in a two wheeler, the Police Officials who were engaged in vehicle checkup,
struck the petitioner's husband in the chest with his lathi and thereby, fell down from the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis bike and he sustained injuries all over the body and then he was taken to the hospital on 16.06.2019, at about 12.15 a.m.
In spite of giving better treatment, he died in the hospital in the evening of 16.06.2019 due to the injuries sustained by him.
The petitioner's husband was aged about 40 years on the date of occurrence and he was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month and he survived with his wife, child and his father as dependants.
The death of the deceased was caused by the fourth respondent while he was engaging his official duty and thereby, all the respondents are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

8.The learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondents 1 to 3 would contend that the petitioner's husband was in a drunken mood and driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, without wearing helmet and without observing traffic rules, came in a high speed at the time when the Police personnels attempted to stop the vehicle and as such, they fell down due to loss of control and thereby themselves invited the incident and the respondents are no way connected in the above said incident.

However, an FIR was registered in Crime No.108 of 2019 and thereafter, the charge sheet was filed as against the fourth respondent and the same is pending for adjudication V.Gajapriya vs The Government Of Tamil Nadu on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9734366/
3 before the trial Court.

sentences.text: In the meantime, the Government has accorded sanction of sum of Rs.3,00,000/- for the deceased family and the same is also under process.
Since the trial is pending before the trial Court, the petitioner has to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis wait till the completion of proceedings.
Therefore, the petition is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed.

9.The learned Counsel appearing for the fourth respondent would contend that the fourth respondent is no way connected in the above said incident and the husband of the petitioner was in a drunken mood and driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and fell down from the bike while the fourth respondent along with other Police Personnel engaged in vehicle checkup duty.
The fourth respondent had discharged his official duty and he has not violated any rules and he is no way responsible for the incident.
Further, already the charge sheet has been filed as against the petitioner and others and the criminal case is also pending before the trial Court.

At this stage,
awarding compensation will affect the criminal case and thereby the petition is liable to be dismissed.

10.This Court has carefully pursued the records, on perusal of records, it is seen that on the date of occurrence, the husband of the deceased came in a two wheeler and the same was stopped by the respondent Police.
At that time, the deceased fell down and sustained injuries and thereafter, died on the next day.

The death of the deceased and cause of death was not denied by the respondents and as per the respondents while they were engaged in a vehicle checkup duty, the husband of the petitioner came in rash and negligent manner https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and he himself fell down by losing his control due to high speed.
Therefore, the respondent is no way responsible for the incident.
However, an FIR has been registered as against the fourth respondent and investigation also completed and charge sheet has been filed and
now the trial is pending.
Since the respondents themselves admitted that the deceased fell down at the time of vehicle check up, and then died, the family of the deceased have to be compensated.
There are prima facie materials available to fasten the liability on the police officials.
The negligence on the part of the fourth respondent, has to be decided by the concerned Court independently based on the available evidence.
At this stage, this Court cannot form any opinion with regard to the negligence on the part of the individual i.e., fourth respondent.
However, the deceased fell down from the two wheeler at the time of vehicle check up and he sustained injuries and then died.
While so, it is the duty of the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner for the death of her husband.

11.The learned Counsel appearing for the respondents 1 to 3 has also argued that the Division Bench of this Court directed to form "one man commission" to fix the quantum of the amount and in support of the Judgment in V.Anandakumar Vs. the District Collector and others in WA.No.4013 of 2019 etc., batch on careful perusal of the above Judgment, it will not be applicable to the present facts of the case because the said case is related to fire accident and so many persons died in the fire accident thereby "one man https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis commission" was appointed by this Court.
12.

sentences.text: In view of the said judgment, this Court is inclined to adopt the multiplier method to award compensation to the petitioner.
13.On careful perusal of the income tax returns of the deceased reveals that he was earning around Rs.2.50 lakhs per year.

Therefore, this Court has taken the income of the deceased as Rs.20,000/-
per month.

The date of birth of the deceased is 07.10.1978 and thereby, he completed the age of 40 years on the date of occurrence and so, future prospects is 25% as per the Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs.Pranay Sethi and others.

Accordingly,
the compensation is determined as under:-
Income per month : Rs.20,000/-, Future prospectus:25%
Monthly income of the deceased would come as 25,000/-(Rs.20,000/-+Rs. 5000/-=25,000/-)
Annual income of the deceased would come to Rs.3,00,000/-(Rs.25,000/- x 12=3,00,000/-)

Considering the dependency of the deceased, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal expenses and thereby, the annual income of the deceased would come Rs.2,00,000/-(Rs.3,00,000/- -Rs. 1,00,000/-=
Rs.2,00,000/-)
By applying the multiplier 15 for the age group of 40 years, the amount would come as Rs.30,00,000/-(Rs.2,00,000 x 15=30,00,000/-).

In addition to above loss of income to the family of the petitioner, under the heads "consortium" -
Rs.48,000/- ; "funeral expenses" - Rs.18,000/- and loss of estate - Rs.18,000/- are granted by this court.

Altogether, the compensation is arrived as follows:-
Rs.30,00,000 + 48,000 + 18,000 + 18,000 = Rs.30,84,000/-

and failed to wear the helmet at the time of accident.
Therefore, this Court deems it fit to deduct 5% from the calculated compensation amount.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.1,54,200/- is deducted.

Considering the dependency of the deceased, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal expenses and thereby, the annual income of the deceased would come Rs.2,00,000/-(Rs.3,00,000/- -Rs. 1,00,000/-=
Rs.2,00,000/-)
By applying the multiplier 15 for the age group of 40 years, the amount would come as Rs.30,00,000/-(Rs.2,00,000 x 15=30,00,000/-).

In addition to above loss of income to the family of the petitioner, under the heads "consortium" -
Rs.48,000/- ; "funeral expenses" - Rs.18,000/- and loss of estate - Rs.18,000/- are granted by this court.

Altogether, the compensation is arrived as follows:-
Rs.30,00,000 + 48,000 + 18,000 + 18,000 = Rs.30,84,000/-
